text:
jamie: Heads-up — we saw a burst of GPU pod evictions in ap-southeast1 ~10:12 UTC. Evictions line up with a network saturation event on a subset of GPU nodes. Not sure if scheduler is overpacking NIC-heavy small pods onto the same racks.

neha: Oof. Any node-level metrics?

jamie: digging, but here's a kubelet log snippet from node gpu-rack-3-12:
```
W0901 10:12:34 kubelet_eviction.go:201] Evicting pod default/training-job-xyz: evicting pods due to imagefs.available< eviction_threshold
W0901 10:12:35 kubelet_disk_manager.go:88] resource pressure: imagefs, ephemeral-storage low
```
Also `sar -n DEV 1 3` showed iface tx spikes to ~950 Mbps on 10Gb link. GPU utilization was high but not maxed; NVLINK okay.

matt: So NIC is pegged and kubelet starts cleaning up pods (disk/net pressure UI?) Could be bulk checkpoints writing to disk + model checkpoints flooding network (S3 gateway)?

li-chen: Are these pods the small inference jobs that use 1 GPU each with high batch network I/O? We recently moved a bunch of cheap inference replicas into the same node class to reduce cost — could be packing side effect.

jamie: Yeah — pods have annotation `redwood.ai/io-bandwidth: high` but scheduler currently ignores that. They were scheduled with strict affinity to GPU type `gpu.a100-40gb` -> ended up co-located.

neha: Suggest short-term mitigations: 1) cordon the worst nodes 2) throttle pod egress with a NodeNetworkPolicy or set a bandwidth limit via CNI 3) add node taint `gpu-net-pressure=true:NoSchedule` when net > 80% via alertmanager webhook.

matt: Agree. What about long-term: scheduler should consider `io-bandwidth` or we should separate instance pools (tiny-gpu-high-net vs tiny-gpu-low-net) so binpacking doesn't mix them. Also consider a plugin that weights by NIC usage not just GPU slots.

li-chen: We can add a cheap heuristic: preferSpreadAcrossRacks for pods annotated with `redwood.ai/io-bandwidth: high` to avoid saturating a single top-of-rack. That avoids immediate infra changes.

jamie: Testing that locally now. Quick experiment: annotate a test deployment and add `podAntiAffinity` to prefer different hosts in different racks.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-2378 - ap-southeast1 GPU pod evictions due to NIC saturation. Page: @oncall. Linked alerts: net.iface.tx > 800Mbps on 10 nodes.

neha: For the cordon step: `kubectl cordon gpu-rack-3-12` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` for the hot nodes, let cyclone re-schedule. We'll avoid mass preempts by draining gradually.

matt: Also check autoscaler: we saw scale-ups at the same time which might be causing temporary overcommit on racks. Could tweak `balance-similar-node-groups` behavior.

li-chen: Long-term design notes:
- expose `redwood.ai/io-bandwidth` node allocatable/offer so scheduler plugin can account for expected egress per pod
- create 2 reserved pools: `gpu-high-net` and `gpu-low-net` (cost tradeoff: high-net instances are slightly more expensive)
- add admission hook to reject packing > N high-net pods per rack

jamie: Quick numbers: estimated additional infra cost if we split pools = ~8% on dev cluster, but saves ~30% evictions and customer retries. Worth it for prod.

neha: Action items:
- jamie: cordon/drain 4 worst nodes now (in progress)
- li-chen: PR to scheduler heuristics (preferSpreadAcrossRacks) draft by EOD
- matt: autoscaler tune rollback to avoid simultaneous rack fill (today's oncall)
- infra: investigate CNI bandwidth shaping as fast mitigation

jamie: cordoned 3 nodes so far, evictions decreased. Still monitoring.

matt: Keep an eye on cross-AZ spillover — if we start scheduling into other AZs we may increase egress costs. Ping finance if we need to enable temp burst capacity.

li-chen: I'll open RFC for `io-aware` scheduler plugin with benchmarks (impact on P95 scheduling latency and pack efficiency).

neha: Nice work team. If cordon/drain stabilizes this, we can roll the node-taint webhook and the temporary scheduler affinity change tomorrow. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Incident INC-2024-2378 update: 3 nodes drained, packet drops down to <1% on affected racks, no new evictions in last 12m.

jamie: closing thread when stable, will attach perf traces and `kubectl describe node` snapshots to the incident.

matt: note: retro idea — add a small per-node synthetic `net_headroom` metric to the control plane telemetry so scheduler heuristics can use it.

li-chen: +1 to net_headroom metric. Will include in RFC.

jamie: thanks all, monitoring continues.
